who-owns-a-registry-fold.text: As a contributor changing a fold, you want the owner of each decision to be clear. The registry owns the state transition and batch transaction. The application owns recognition of a pending request, its spending script and its approval burn. The folder supplies public chain data and its own wallet.

from-a-pending-request-to-a-batch.text: From a pending request to a batch.

The fold discovers pending requests through the application adapter and checks each against the selected registry and trie. Automatic selection skips individually unfoldable requests and keeps the first foldable request for each key. An explicitly selected batch is built in the requested order or refused; it is never silently trimmed.

The lineage owner reconstructs the registry trie from public history. The assembly owner constructs state continuation, request spends, token effects, committed holdings, rewards, validity and collateral. The application adapter supplies request recognition and spending rules. No booker's local file is an input to the fold.

choices-and-verification-limits.text: The state-fold and application request-fold suites exercise the current builders against compiled validators and altered-input controls. The packaged journey checks connected registration, update and termination on a private development chain. These are separate evidence boundaries; see the consumer record for requirements still uncovered.
Browse the generated API reference for signatures and source, and the command guide for caller-visible receipts and selection behavior.
